findings.finding: The founder's brief names the product 'L-Shaped Memory-Foam Forearm & Wrist Desk Rest Pad' and describes the supplier's sample as a memory-foam pad, and all four rival titles carry 'Memory Foam' (F1, F5, F7, F11). The version that will be sampled, v1_lean = innovaty v1_now (I1, I3, I5, I6), contains no memory foam at all: one HR polyether core at 50 kg/m3, 25% IFD 150-190 N, which springs back at once and is 'firmer at first touch than a slow-sinking memory-foam wrist rest' (innovaty honest_limitations[2]). Innovaty's title honestly omits the words, which also drops the one keyword every tile on 'elbow pad for desk' shares. Nothing is wrong with the engineering choice (it is the right answer to C1's creep and bottoming), but nobody has told the founder that the sample they are about to order is not the product their brief names, that the listing cannot say 'memory foam' without a claims problem, and that the memory-foam version is I2 at about +$0.55 a set in v1.1. That is a before-samples decision, not a text fix (law.benefit_not_feature, sharp.mental_availability, gate.title_scan).
findings.fix: Orchestrator puts the choice to the founder in one line before the T1 sample is ordered: ship v1 as a high-resilience (not memory-foam) pad under a name and title without 'memory foam', accepting the keyword loss and the firmer touch as the stated limitation; or pull I2 forward now (HR core under a 10 mm memory shell, +$0.55 a set, cradle and peel gate) so the name, the keyword and the brief agree. Record the answer in brief.assumptions and, if the first, rename brief.product_name.

findings.finding: The 'sign nothing until' gate is restated as necessary-not-sufficient (K3 of pass 1, resolved), but its arithmetic uses two different freight numbers. The base landed ($8.70) adds freight $1.25 'assumes a 1,000-set order' + inbound $0.45 + reserve $0.40 = $2.10 of non-EXW adders; the gate's 'EXW <= $4.50 at MOQ 1,000 and 26% puts v1_lean at $7.25-7.40, under the $7.50 rail' only works with $1.70 of adders (4.50 x 1.26 = 5.67 + 1.70 = 7.37), i.e. freight at about $0.85. With the base adders the gate lands at $7.77, over the rail, and the EXW that actually clears $7.50 at 26% is about $4.30. Then, taking every lever at the best end genius names (EXW $4.50, 26%, landed $7.40, the box held to the 1.25-1.5 lb row at $5.10, ads at 15%, returns 6%): 24.99 - 3.75 - 5.10 - 0.46 - 3.75 - 0.87 - 7.40 = $3.66, which is 14.6% of price, still under the engine's 15% floor, and 27-29.5% before advertising, under the founder's own 30-40%. The file implies the floor is reachable in year two; by its own numbers it is missed by half a point at the best combination (forecast.fermi, gate.price_vs_anchor).
findings.fix: State the adders the gate uses (freight at 1,000 sets, inbound, reserve) in premortem[6] and make the base's freight assumption agree with them, or reset the gate to EXW <= $4.30 at MOQ 1,000; add the one-line contribution arithmetic at the gate (pre-ad and at 15% ads) to premortem[6] and three_sentences[2], and say plainly that the honest steady state at $24.99 is 10-14.6% after ads and 27-29.5% before, with no named lever that lifts it past 15%.

findings.finding: Genius still describes the recommended lean core as a '60 kg/m3' core in five places: bom[0] ('about 70 g at 60 kg/m3', priced as viscoelastic at $4.5-7/kg), premortem[0] ('the single 60 kg/m3 core took a permanent dent'), premortem[2] ('cap pad weight at 200 g with the 60 kg/m3 build'), idea_rulings[I2] ('over one 60 kg/m3 core') and three_sentences[1] ('with one 60 kg/m3 core'). Innovaty's lean core (I1, I5 tag, moat_built_in, durability_review) is HR polyether at 50 kg/m3 (45-55), which at 1,170 cm3 weighs about 58 g a pad, not 70, and whose five-year failure is fatigue softening (<= 20% hardness loss), not the compression-set dent of memory foam that premortem[0] writes the obituary for. The woven tag will print 50 kg/m3 while the founder's three sentences say 60. The gates in premortem[0]'s mitigation are the right ones; the obituary and the spec line are of the previous build (forecast.premortem, cialdini.authority).
findings.fix: Replace 60 kg/m3 with 'HR 50 kg/m3 (45-55), 25% IFD 150-190 N' in all five places; price bom[0] as HR slab at $3-5/kg over about 58 g plus waste (the range can stay, the reasoning cannot); rewrite premortem[0]'s obituary as 'softened 20% at the roll after a summer and the arm found the corner' so the ISO 3385 hardness-loss gate is the one it names.

findings.finding: C1 is 'too thin OR too firm; still feel the edge'. The lean single core is gated against thin (edge-load bottoming >= 8 mm residual, compression set, fatigue) and I1's 'reassures' is honest for what the buyer's shape memory reads: no fold, continuous foam over the corner, visible spring-back, a density number (law.shape_memory). But 'too firm' has no gate at all. A 150-190 N IFD HR core at 20-26 mm under a bony ulna is a medium-firm seat grade on a thin layer, innovaty itself says above 55 kg/m3 or 190 N it 'reads as hard under the ulna', honest_limitations[2] admits the firmer first touch, and the goniometer test measures wrist angle, not pressure. The only triggers that pull I2 forward are bottoming, set and fatigue, so a T1 sample that reads hard under the elbow has no path in the plan except a one-star review (kano.must_be, post.review_trigger).
findings.fix: Add a comfort gate to I1's test on the T1 sample: peak interface pressure under a 25 mm ulna simulant at 30 N on the roll (or, cheaper, a five-user 60-minute blind panel against a JIKIOU and a VAYDEER pad with a stated pass rule such as no user rating it harder than the VAYDEER), and make failing it a third unlock trigger for I2 in version_plan and genius premortem[0]. Genius adds the $50-150 to the foam lab line.

findings.finding: The lab budget and the lab-gate phase still run 'ISO 6330 20 washes' on a cover that innovaty has sewn closed and says is never washed (I1, I3 fit_range, honest_limitations[1]); that was I4's test and I4 is v1.1. Meanwhile innovaty's durability_review names the fixed knit over the roll as the single weakest point and writes its only gate in changes_made[0]: Martindale abrasion >= 20,000 cycles (ISO 12947-2), pilling >= 3-4 (ISO 12945-2) and the 14-day sebum tack and odour test on the fixed knit, plus the base panel's 50 damp-wipe cycles and 30 d at 40 C / 80% RH (changes_made[2]). None of the abrasion or wipe gates is in genius's lab line or the timeline, so the weakest point of the recommended build has no budgeted proof while an irrelevant wash test does (law.shape_memory, cialdini.authority).
findings.fix: In tooling_and_nre[5] and timeline phase 3, replace the 20-wash test with Martindale abrasion and pilling on the knit lot and the 50 damp-wipe / humidity test on the base panel; keep the sebum ageing; the cost is within the same $350-1,400 range.

findings.finding: Three places still say v1_lean's idea_ids 'are NOT innovaty's v1_now (I1-I6)' and that 'the orchestrator must reconcile innovaty's image 3 (two-band section) and image 4 (unzip step) before anything is shot'. Verified against the current innovaty: version_plan.v1_now is exactly I1, I3, I5, I6, image brief 2 shows one band of foam, image brief 4 shows a wipe, the packaging prompt says 'no zip or opening anywhere', and no v1 field carries I2, I4 or I7 content. The reconciliation is done; the founder's second sentence instructs an action already taken.
findings.fix: Delete the reconcile clauses in the three places and say instead that innovaty's v1_now and the recommended version agree.

findings.finding: The sectioned pad beside the ruler is image 2 in image_briefs_2_to_4[0] and in pillars.uniqueness, but I5 says 'image 3 is a thumb-on-ruler sectioned pad' and its tag text is legible 'in the image-3 close-up next to the sectioned sample', while brief[1] makes image 3 the hard case (eased edge, bare base on glass). Genius premortem[1] cites both ('image 2's ruler' and 'image 3's sectioned pad'). The photographer gets two shot lists.

three_things_the_founder_must_hear: The engine's numbers at the recommended lean set, $24.99: landed $8.70 (34.8% of price), the fee stack $17.12 a set (referral $3.75, FBA $5.75 for a 71 mm-tall L that can never be small-standard, storage $0.46, ads $6.25, returns $0.91), contribution -$0.83 a set (-3.3%), 0 of 10,000 simulated first years profitable, median -$19k, and -$17k under the clone wave because when every set loses money, selling fewer loses less. The engine already calls that unrealistic; what this pass adds is that the gate you were given does not fix it either: $4.50 EXW at MOQ 1,000 on the 26% line lands at $7.77 with the plan's own freight (not $7.40), and with every lever at its best end (box in the 1.25-1.5 lb row, ads down to 15% after 100 reviews, returns 6%) the set makes 14.6% after advertising and 27-29.5% before it, under the engine's 15% floor and under your 30-40%. The single fact that moves the money most is the MOQ-1,000 EXW in writing ($4.00 against $4.80 is $1.00 a set landed); the tariff line is worth $0.56 (26% against 13.5%) and the box row $0.65; none of them alone, and not all three together, lifts this past 15% at $24.99 from China.

The design is genuinely good, and it is consistent now. The geometry checks: 26 mm legs with the R20 roll centred 6 mm outboard puts the roll 28.5 mm from the inside corner on the diagonal, minus the 6 mm relief leaves about 22 mm of continuous HR foam over the desk corner where every 2-pack on the page has a fabric fold and nothing; the 26-to-20 mm wedge is 3.4 degrees with the foam at the edge, not the keys; the same numbers sit in I1, the durability review, the title (0.8-1 in), the image briefs and all three prompts, and no v1 field still shows the memory shell, the zip or the magnets. One vulcanised rubber sheet on both faces with nothing adhesive in the box, a tag that prints a density and a two-year flatten-or-peel Limited Warranty, aired foam and no bag: that is the magic, and it is a $200-1,100 cutting template, not a steel mould. The picture that sells it is the one the buyer described before anyone drew it: a bare forearm over a thick desk edge with daylight under it, and a sectioned pad next to a ruler.

Two things to settle before the T1 sample is ordered, then three text fixes. First: v1 is not a memory-foam pad. It is a high-resilience core that springs back and feels firmer at first touch, your brief names the product 'Memory-Foam', every rival title says 'Memory Foam', and your listing honestly cannot; say yes to that knowingly, or pull I2 forward at about +$0.55 a set. Second: C1 is 'too thin or too firm', and the plan tests only thin; add a pressure or five-user comfort gate on the sample so a pad that reads hard under the elbow has a path other than a one-star. Then: genius still calls the core 60 kg/m3 in five places while the tag will print 50; the lab budget runs a 20-wash test on a cover that is never washed and skips the abrasion test on the fabric the durability review names as the weakest point; and the gate arithmetic needs one freight number, not two.
